Pure Inbred

By: Sasha OLD | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When you buy a pedigree and purebred pup you believe you are buying the best and healthiest dogs - but our investigation shows that is not the case.

Unique Selling Point:
We are going to be looking the entire industry - from breeding and how it began in Victorian England times, to the dog shows which award breeders with best in show awards for certain bred attributes - which are unhealthy for the dog, to the breeders - both unethical and ethical, and then to the regulator of the industry KUSA. We will interview numerous case studies and go undercover to show the real way this industry works. Based on the UK documentary's which exposed this industry on the UK kennel club, who established these breeds. This is going to rock our audience's socks off - because what you thought was healthy and wonderful - will turn your perception of this world on its head.

Summary:
Riddled with genetic disease
Dog breeds aren’t even a real thing – like nature created them that way, and that every mutt is a mix of pure breeds.
Like: 1,5 retriever, sheepdog, 1/6 poodle, chow? German shepherd, 1/12 border collie
So they are selectively bred for their traits – 90% of all dog breeds were created the past 100 years.
In 19th century Victorian era, competitive dog breeding became all the rage…then they declared it a pure breed. Inbred – never allowed to mate outside of species.
One study found that 10,000 pugs have the same genetic diversity as 50 individuals – making them highly inbred. This leads to them being often sick. 60% of golden retrievers die of cancer, 1/3 of spaniel’s have skulls too small for their brains. Great Danes are so huge now that their hearts can’t support their bodies.
Bulldog – so cute – total genetic failure. A century of inbreeding has ruined them, noses are so squashed they can barely breathe, their heads are so big they can only give birth by caesarean section, their tails have become ingrown, they basically all have hip dysplasia and their average life expectancy is 6 years – these dogs shouldn’t be alive. But they win things like “best in show.” Kennel clubs could fix their problems if they cross breed, but they won’t because then they won’t be as cute. It’s our existence that is letting them live up to our arbitrary existence.
Easy solution – go to shelter.

Further information:
EXPERT study: Responsible breeders are those that make the welfare of each animal and its offspring their first priority. These breeders participate in genetic health improvement schemes such as hip and elbow improvement schemes and test their dogs to detect carriers of known genetic disorders.
The negative publicity of unethical breeders tarnishes the credibility of those who are ethical.
Breeder often feel they have tried their utmost to test for genetic defects, and feel they have to defend themselves against unfair claims and feel despondent.
There is an ongoing onslaught against some of these bodies because of claims that their breed standards blatantly oppose health, rather than promote it – the reluctance to change these breed standards stems from the fact that changing features in dogs may threaten the very existence of the breed in its current form.
Breeding strategies that involve judging on the production of over-exaggerated conformational features have attracted severe criticism – but there are breeders who have courageously suggested drastic changes to some breed standards.
English + French Bulldog - brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome. When dogs with these extreme phenotypes are delivered by caesarean section, there is no motivations for selection against this aesthetic and hence the associated morbidity and mortality rates will increase.
Selection for healthier conformation should be the first aim – some say that for the maximum wellbeing of future generations, we should abandon the most predisposed breeds while loosening the genetic barriers between the remaining breeds to promote genetic variability. In a recent study 48% of vets were advising clients against purchasing a predigree dog due to inherited disorders – but not all deleterious traits should be attributed to breed standards, and mix breeds can also have genetic disorders.
Unfortunately fashion and social influence are more important than function in determining the popularity of dog breeds – designer dogs like the labradoodle – Labrador and poodle have a misconception that because they are originated from distinct breeds, they will automatically be healthier and less prone to inherited disorders, in fact they will only be as healthy as the founding stock, and are likely to suffer from the conditions prevalent in the founding breeds.
In 2016, the USA has the largest number of registered puppies with numbers approaching the one million per year mark, while the UK has roughly 250,000. South Africa is vastly outnumbered by these stats as only 22,000 with the Boerboel and English bulldog topping the list. Given these numbers its no surprise that we have a limited role to play in funding research towards developing tests and genetic progress in general. For example – Hip Dysplasia is a serious orthopaedic condition causing major discomfort to pet, huge vetinary bills for owners and is the most common problem amongst local breeds. Despite this problem KUSA only have 7 breeds which have restrictions for hip dysplasia. A local study on Rottweilers (do have breeding restrictions) and Labrador retrievers (don’t have breeding restrictions) proved that prescribing minimum breeding requirements significantly improved the breeding stock.
Issues: Dog registries depend on puppy registration fees for their survival and cannot impose restrictions in the absence of significant support from their members for such a proposal. (BUT SURELY THEY SHOULD GROW SOME BALLS) Some say by imposing restrictions the public form the opinion that that breed is unhealthy.
Open heath data base register – shows dogs lineages that have been tested – make it open which is opposed by breeders because if they have a negative result they’ll be stigmatized.

COSTS:
5 days shooting: 3 days with Derek, 4 in Joburg, 1 in Cape Town.
4 DAYS of shooting: Each day of shooting:
Camera-man roughly R4,500 (subject to availability), if we want a drone, or his slider – which is awesome for sitdown boring interviews it’s R5,000 for Peter. X 4 days – roughly R18,000-R20,000
Camera assistant/ sound roughly R2,000 – R2,500. (subject to availability) X4 days = Roughly R8,000-10,000
1 day extra for camera – Ben will let us take his for R1200. We have lights so we don’t need to rent that. For that day I would like to take Sinethemba to assist me, otherwise we need to hire an assistant. I won’t have a presenter.
Flight to Cape Town: If I can have a few days off to spend time with my mom including weekend, then I can pay half for flight. We also don’t pay for accommodation. Just vehicle mileage of me or camera man’s car. Roughly R2,800-R3,200 (half is R1400 to R1,600)
Food: for 4 people: as per Nikola R100 pp. for 4 days. Need likely additional R200 for snacks for the duration of the shoot – nuts and fruit. +R200 for Sinethemba and I are extra with camera. R2,000.
Car hire: not sure what that price usually is? But in Cape Town which is one of the days, I’ll ask the camera man to just use his mileage. Peter is unhappy to use his car, because he was attacked, and R3,50 wasn’t enough for him. So… likely 3 days car hire. I’d like to book the CAP car for the day I shoot with Sinethemba + car hire for now for 3 days.
Editor: We are trying use Bryan, even if it’s for offline. Usually a 20 minuter requires 4 days edit, and depending on documents, 2 days online. That was my previous experience, but it was document heavy. I don’t expect this to be. If Bryan can assist with some of it then I think 2 days with him, and 2-3 with Floris. Floris costs R3,600 (special rate for me – and tax is reported to SARS, and comes back to CAP during tax season.) X3 days = R10,800 for Floris. If it’s Jan, I think it’s R4000. So that’s R12,000
Graphic day = R4,500 for graphics to be created by Ethniks. I will need some complicated graphics potentially, so I’m flagging it now. It would be to show the breeding standards, an explanation of how breeders breed, and how a dog is bred for certain traits. I’ve used Owen, he’s also usually happy to drop his rate for me…
Audio Mix: Usually take a full day because it’s double the amount of time. R1,026 per hour. Rob usually takes 4 hours for 10 minutes. So R8,208 for the day. I can also chat to rob and make sure he doesn’t go over. I will keep you informed if there any audio issues, but I haven’t had any in the past (touch wood)
So roughly: R50, 908 at the maximums of all those figures above. + car hire + Sasha Fuel (which has not been included). For the higher costs Wynand intimated it would be a longer story. I asked for 20 minutes, but obviously it depends on the stuff we have. So far it’s very strong. Please see attached Excel Spreadsheet.

Press Release:


Pedigree Dogs
They’re cute, from a distinguished bloodline and they fetch a hefty price tag. But with selective breeding for specific and special traits, are pedigreed puppies really healthy? Carte Blanche investigates a breeding industry that has created dogs with chronic illnesses and health problems passed on from litter to litter – costing you thousands in vet bills.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender


Script:


Meet Fabio Waldron …(Breathing heavily…)*
CW: “He’s a complex broken little boy. with an unbelievable passion for life.”
Owner Christine Waldron always wanted a cute french bulldog. But Fabio came with numerous genetic disorders.
CW: “He's had 4 nose surgerys, two hips, neck surgery, eyelashes, his throat, elongated palate and glandial sacheals.”
Fabio cost R15,000, but Christine has spent over a quarter of a million rands in Vet’s bills and he’s not even 4 years old. Fabio is registered with the Kennel Union of Southern Africa or KUSA - the most prestigious local pedigree registry.
LINK: THE WORD ‘PEDIGREE’ REFERS TO A DOCUMENT THAT STATES THE DOGS LINEAGE BUT, THIS IS BY NO MEANS A GUARANTEE OF QUALITY. IT SIMPLY MEANS THAT THE DOG’S RECORDS ARE ON FILE AND HIS BLOODLINE GOING BACK THREE OR FIVE GENERATIONS IS TRACEABLE.
The French bulldog is one of several brachycephalic breeds - which means its skull is shorter than what’s typical for the canine species.
Dr de cramer: “Brachycephalic just means basically a squashed in nose.”
Veterinarian Dr. Kurt De Cramer specializes in canine reproduction.
Devi: “Those dogs snore a lot?”
De Cramer: They’ve got pinched in nostrils, they’ve got small tracheas and many other features that restrict their airways.”
Some owners feed them in a baby's high chair to stop stomach acid from burning their throats. Fabio’s owner turned to Dale Neves who rescues bulldogs to help with Fabio.
Dale: “People seem to normalize these dogs health issues, but it’s really the dog suffering and battling to breathe.”
Dale had gone to great lengths to find a reputable breeder - and her pup was KUSA registered.
Dale: “Finally I got my ﬁrst french bulldog, unbeknownst to myself he had various health issues, my ﬁrst frenchie only lived to the age of 3.”
Dr. DC: “That dog cannot survive in nature. We did this by natural selection, as I say it was for the cute factor.”
This is because bulldogs and some other breeds cannot procreate by themselves.
Dr. DC: “The existence of certain breeds are questioned because the caesarean section rate in Bulldogs approaches almost 100%.”
Online video clips from breeders show how dog semen is collected to artificially inseminate females, who later deliver via caesarean section - often several in their lifetime.
Dr. DC: “And this creates an ethical conundrum for the veterinary fraternity because we cant refuse to do these cesarean sections.”
With an average lifespan of only 6 years, English bulldogs are known as the most unhealthy breed. But, they are now ranked the most popular KUSA pedigree breed.
LINK: “BREEDING HEALTHY PEDIGREE PUPPIES IS A COSTLY BUSINESS – SO YOU COULD EASILY PAY BETWEEN R10,000 AND SOMETIMES EVEN AS MUCH AS R70,000 FOR A PUPPY!”
Dale: “The perception is when you get a purebred dog, that the dog is healthy, that all the necessary health tests have been done, and that the KUSA breeders are the most ethical.”
But Dale believes some unethical breeders hide behind KUSA’s reputation.

Dale: “Anybody who would like to breed can go pay a small fee, they could choose their kennel name without having any knowledge of breeding.”
Pedigree puppies sell for thousands online. But the KUSA registered ones come at an even higher premium.
LINK: AS DOGS ARE ALL THE SAME SPECIES, THE BREEDS CAN MIX. BUT SEARCHING FOR SPECIFIC GENETIC TRAITS LIKE THE “SMUSHED FACE” IS WHY THESE ANIMALS WERE INBRED TO CREATE A LOOK, THEIR WOLF ANCESTORS MIGHT NOT EVEN RECOGNISE AS CANINE.
Each purebred dog needs to conform to a breed standard which is judged at shows
Devi: “Hello! What a cutie pie. What Shampoo does she use, it’s probably more expensive than my shampoo.”
[3 seconds of devi at the show]
June DW: “A reputable breeder is there to improve the breed, not just a money making concern.”
Dalmation breeder June de Wet has been showing her dogs for 27 years.
Jdw: “Kusa is the first step - owners need to do their homework.”
Cheryl Jacobs breeds Rhodesian ridgebacks. She knows unethical breeders would put a perfectly healthy pup down if it doesn’t conform to the breed standard.
Cheryl Jacobs: “I have had ridgeless, I do not euthanize them, I do sell them at a reduced price and i sell them as pets.”
Dr. Quixi Sonntag teaches veterinary science at the University of Pretoria and used to breed and show dogs.
Dr. QT: “I started realizing the main interest was not that of the dogs themselves, they wanted their dogs to win, so that they could look good.”
Devi: “So is it a myth that if you buy a purebred puppy it will be healthier?”
DR QS: “It’s not a guarantee that a purebred puppy will be healthier than a mixed breed.”
LINK: “IN THE PAST 100 YEARS , 90% OF ALL BREEDS WERE “CREATED” BY BREEDING THEM FOR SPECIFIC TRAITS. WHEN IT COMES TO THE BRACHYCEPHALIC BREEDS, THE CREATION OF THOSE CUTE SQUISHED NOSES WAS ACTUALLY A DEFORMITY THAT CAME ABOUT BY GENETICALLY CRISS-CROSSING SOME BREEDS AND THEN INBREEDING THOSE DOGS RESULTING IN THE FACIAL AND NASAL DEFORMITY.”
De cramer: “Show ofﬁcials ensure that the breeds indeed conform to the standard - however, there’s many indiv who would say that breed standards in some cases oppose health features.”
LINK: THERE IS AN ONGOING BATTLE AGAINST SOME OF THESE REGISTRY BODIES BECAUSE OF CLAIMS THAT THEIR BREED STANDARDS BLATANTLY OPPOSE HEALTH, RATHER THAN PROMOTE IT – THEIR RELUCTANCE TO CHANGE THESE BREED STANDARDS STEMS FROM THE FACT THAT CHANGING FEATURES IN DOGS MAY THREATEN THE VERY EXISTENCE OF THE BREED IN ITS CURRENT FORM.
For example the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, bred for a small flat head, is prone to brain damage where the dog scratches and cries out in pain.
Dachshunds are bred for length, which can lead to disc and spinal problems.
Meg: “When somebody is making money off of this, it’s a commodity, all it needs to do is breed more animals.”
NSPCA Spokesperson Meg Wilson says many pedigree dogs become their problem.
Meg: “In an overpopulated society why are we encouraging this?”
Devi: “Do you think we are obsessed with pedigree dogs and designer dog?”
Meg: “I think some people do it for status and they don’t necessarily realize what’s happened behind the scenes.”
Vicky Finnemore of the Benoni SPCA responded to a tip off about animal health concerns at a breeder in Johannesburg.
VF: “We removed 45 animals with cancerous tumours that had burst open, dental diseases, emaciated dogs that could barely walk, 13 of the dogs had to be put down straight away. The owners of these dogs are international show breed judges, they also breed KUSA registered dogs and sell them to the public.”
Francesca and Jackie Browning co-own Braganza and breed poodles, cocker spaniels - and the designer combo - “cocker-poodles” that sell for six to ten thousand rands.
Devi: “Did that surprise you?”
VF: “No, we have been on plenty cruelty complaints of kusa registered dogs involved.”
The Brownings were charged with animal cruelty and neglect, and have been suspended by KUSA.
LINK: UNFORTUNATELY, THESE DOGS CAN’T BE ADOPTED UNTIL THE CASE IS FINALIZED AND THAT COULD TAKE YEARS, AND IF THE BROWNINGS ARE FOUND NOT GUILTY, THEN THESE ANIMALS WILL BE RETURNED TO THEM.
As the matter is on-going the Brownings declined an interview.
UPSOUND: Jacky: “Our statement at this moment in time, is no comment.”
Viewers submitted complaints about purebred puppies which have cost them thousands in vet bills, so we investigated some breeders.
The first was Sezer Kennels in Randburg, which breeds and shows English bulldogs. It was owned by Arthur Seeff. Photos from 2015 showed injured and dead dogs, leading to animal welfare stepping in and arthur complying with their concerns.
Now we received viewers complaints with photos of dogs with serious health issues, spanning the last 20 years:
● Napoleon, and Wellington had spinal issues that led to both being put down,
● Clementine died when her trachea collapsed,
● Patches had severe hip dysplasia and was put down,
● And Jessebel's spinal issues have paralysed her.
We paid them a visit undercover.
Journalist: “So your dogs are very healthy?”
Arthur: ‘We have not got a sick dog on the property and we’ve got 80 dogs here.”
Sezer Kennels registers puppies like Arabella with KUSA.
A: “This is the girl, but I need her for breeding.”
Once Arabella’s show days are over, she’s destined to be bred regularly, just like her mother.
Journalist: “How often do they mate?”
Arthur: “6 months.”
KUSA and several experts say continual breeding is unethical because it doesn’t allow the mother to recover from repeated caesareans.
We asked Arthur for an interview:
UPSOUND: Arthur Seeff: “I’m in and out of hospital, I’m not in the best frame of mind.”
We halted the story to give Arthur time to get well, but he subsequently passed away and there’s been no further comment from his family.
Beverlander is another breeding facility selling KUSA registered French and English bulldogs. Our viewers complained that their Randfontein operation owned by Alta Wilters produces puppies with serious genetic issues - like Winston whose long list of health problems resulted in his death before his first birthday. A caring dog lover took in these 5 dogs because they all suffered from a number of different genetic defects - including swimmer syndrome.
Wilters declined an on-camera interview, but said that Beverlander isn’t a puppy mill and that the SPCA has found nothing wrong with her dogs’ living conditions.
The SPCA says it can do little about the continuous breeding of dogs with genetic disorders. Wilters says she’s one of many breeders dealing with inherent genetic defects of specific breeds.
AW: “Am I the only person that that happens to? That dog, it can be in the surroundings where she picked up that sickness.”
KUSA’s general manager Pascale Midgley says they’re regulated by the department of agriculture.
Pascale Midgley: “There is no such thing as a kusa breeder, we do not license someone to say that you are a breeder.”
Devi: “Can anyone breed?”
Pascale: “No one can stop anybody from having a litter. The Kennel Union has registered 178,000 dogs over the last 10 years. If we impose very very strict requirements all that happens is that ppl stop registering.”
Devi: “As a registry, it’s not your responsibility to go out check facilities?
PM: “Under animal improvement act we don’t have that jurisdiction.
Devi: “But dogs are your currency you’re not looking necessarily after the welfare of the dogs?”
PM: “We not an animal welfare organization, we support them when necessary.”
Devi: “Should we not look at changing those breed standards
PM: “So the breed standards are evolving, and we automatically adopt those changes.”
LINK: ONE STUDY BY THE IMPERIAL COLLEGE OF LONDON SHOWED THAT THE 10,000 PUGS IN THE UK, THEY’RE SO INBRED, THAT THEIR GENE POOL IS THE EQUIVALENT OF ONLY 50 INDIVIDUALS.
Canine Geneticist Mischa Fraser of Inqaba laboratory specializes in testing for genetic conditions.
MF: “Something that is inherited, is inherited from mother or father to child. So a genetic disease might be inherited.”
The lab has developed 700 possible genetic tests that a breeder can use.
MF: “We're very involved with many breeders and a breeder will often come and tell me this is the test I'm interested in.”
There are ethical breeders like June and Cheryl who are KUSA members and do test their breeding stock to ensure the healthiest dogs possible are bred- but there are no guarantees.
To curb bad breeding practices KUSA’s is designing an enhanced registration certificate that shows a puppy has been genetically tested.
De Cramer would like to take it a step further: Having an online health registration database with genetic testing results.
Dr. DC: “The breeding authorities should still take courageous steps to try and make a lot of things mandatory so that the public out there you know have some sort of a minimum guarantee.”
LINK: IN 2017, THE UK’S ANIMAL WELFARE LEGISLATION CHANGED TO INCLUDE A NEW LAW WHICH WILL ALLOW FOR THE PROSECUTION OF BREEDERS WHO KNOWINGLY PRODUCE UNHEALTHY PUPPIES AND KITTENS WITH GENETIC DEFECTS. THIS EFFECTIVELY CREATES THE CRIME OF “QUALZUCHT” OR TORTURE BREEDING .
But since South Africa has no laws against unethical breeding practices, Dale Neves set up a bulldog breeding council to help breeders test their breeding stock.
Dale: “We are not expecting the breeders to have dogs that are completely healthy, but don't then onsell a dog knowing full well that you’ve bred a dog with hereditary diseases.”
Fabio will undergo a lifetime of acupuncture and water therapy sessions to rebuild muscle so he can walk properly.
Devi: “Getting a puppy is too much of an impulse purchase?”
DR QS: “Yes, it’s an emotional decision, what they don’t realize is that they're supporting that business, and they just made it possible for that breeder to make money. So why will they stop breeding?”
THE END

Unfortunately fashion and social influence are more important than function in determining the popularity of dog breeds – designer dogs like the labradoodle – Labrador and poodle have a misconception that because they are originated from distinct breeds, they will automatically be healthier and less prone to inherited disorders, in fact they will only be as healthy as the founding stock, and are likely to suffer from the conditions prevalent in the founding breeds. Despite this problem KUSA only have 7 breeds which have restrictions for hip dysplasia. A local study on Rottweilers (do have breeding restrictions) and Labrador retrievers (don’t have breeding restrictions) proved that prescribing minimum breeding requirements significantly improved the breeding stock. Release: Pedigree Dogs They’re cute, from a distinguished bloodline and they fetch a hefty price tag. But with selective breeding for specific and special traits, are pedigreed puppies really healthy? Carte Blanche investigates a breeding industry that has created dogs with chronic illnesses and health problems passed on from litter to litter – costing you thousands in vet bills. Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender Script: Meet Fabio Waldron …(Breathing heavily…)* CW: “He’s a complex broken little boy. with an unbelievable passion for life.” Owner Christine Waldron always wanted a cute french bulldog. But Fabio came with numerous genetic disorders. CW: “He's had 4 nose surgerys, two hips, neck surgery, eyelashes, his throat, elongated palate and glandial sacheals.” Fabio cost R15,000, but Christine has spent over a quarter of a million rands in Vet’s bills and he’s not even 4 years old. Fabio is registered with the Kennel Union of Southern Africa or KUSA - the most prestigious local pedigree registry. LINK: THE WORD ‘PEDIGREE’ REFERS TO A DOCUMENT THAT STATES THE DOGS LINEAGE BUT, THIS IS BY NO MEANS A GUARANTEE OF QUALITY. IT SIMPLY MEANS THAT THE DOG’S RECORDS ARE ON FILE AND HIS BLOODLINE GOING BACK THREE OR FIVE GENERATIONS IS TRACEABLE. The French bulldog is one of several brachycephalic breeds - which means its skull is shorter than what’s typical for the canine species. Dr de cramer: “Brachycephalic just means basically a squashed in nose.” Veterinarian Dr. Kurt De Cramer specializes in canine reproduction. Devi: “Those dogs snore a lot?” De Cramer: They’ve got pinched in nostrils, they’ve got small tracheas and many other features that restrict their airways.” Some owners feed them in a baby's high chair to stop stomach acid from burning their throats. Fabio’s owner turned to Dale Neves who rescues bulldogs to help with Fabio. Dale: “People seem to normalize these dogs health issues, but it’s really the dog suffering and battling to breathe.” Dale had gone to great lengths to find a reputable breeder - and her pup was KUSA registered. Dale: “Finally I got my ﬁrst french bulldog, unbeknownst to myself he had various health issues, my ﬁrst frenchie only lived to the age of 3.” Dr. DC: “That dog cannot survive in nature. We did this by natural selection, as I say it was for the cute factor.” This is because bulldogs and some other breeds cannot procreate by themselves. Dr. DC: “The existence of certain breeds are questioned because the caesarean section rate in Bulldogs approaches almost 100%.” Online video clips from breeders show how dog semen is collected to artificially inseminate females, who later deliver via caesarean section - often several in their lifetime. Dr. DC: “And this creates an ethical conundrum for the veterinary fraternity because we cant refuse to do these cesarean sections.” With an average lifespan of only 6 years, English bulldogs are known as the most unhealthy breed. But, they are now ranked the most popular KUSA pedigree breed. LINK: “BREEDING HEALTHY PEDIGREE PUPPIES IS A COSTLY BUSINESS – SO YOU COULD EASILY PAY BETWEEN R10,000 AND SOMETIMES EVEN AS MUCH AS R70,000 FOR A PUPPY!” Dale: “The perception is when you get a purebred dog, that the dog is healthy, that all the necessary health tests have been done, and that the KUSA breeders are the most ethical.” But Dale believes some unethical breeders hide behind KUSA’s reputation. Dale: “Anybody who would like to breed can go pay a small fee, they could choose their kennel name without having any knowledge of breeding.” Pedigree puppies sell for thousands online. But the KUSA registered ones come at an even higher premium. LINK: AS DOGS ARE ALL THE SAME SPECIES, THE BREEDS CAN MIX. BUT SEARCHING FOR SPECIFIC GENETIC TRAITS LIKE THE “SMUSHED FACE” IS WHY THESE ANIMALS WERE INBRED TO CREATE A LOOK, THEIR WOLF ANCESTORS MIGHT NOT EVEN RECOGNISE AS CANINE. Each purebred dog needs to conform to a breed standard which is judged at shows Devi: “Hello! What a cutie pie. What Shampoo does she use, it’s probably more expensive than my shampoo.” [3 seconds of devi at the show] June DW: “A reputable breeder is there to improve the breed, not just a money making concern.” Dalmation breeder June de Wet has been showing her dogs for 27 years. Jdw: “Kusa is the first step - owners need to do their homework.” Cheryl Jacobs breeds Rhodesian ridgebacks. She knows unethical breeders would put a perfectly healthy pup down if it doesn’t conform to the breed standard. Cheryl Jacobs: “I have had ridgeless, I do not euthanize them, I do sell them at a reduced price and i sell them as pets.” Dr. Quixi Sonntag teaches veterinary science at the University of Pretoria and used to breed and show dogs. Dr. QT: “I started realizing the main interest was not that of the dogs themselves, they wanted their dogs to win, so that they could look good.” Devi: “So is it a myth that if you buy a purebred puppy it will be healthier?” DR QS: “It’s not a guarantee that a purebred puppy will be healthier than a mixed breed.” LINK: “IN THE PAST 100 YEARS , 90% OF ALL BREEDS WERE “CREATED” BY BREEDING THEM FOR SPECIFIC TRAITS. WHEN IT COMES TO THE BRACHYCEPHALIC BREEDS, THE CREATION OF THOSE CUTE SQUISHED NOSES WAS ACTUALLY A DEFORMITY THAT CAME ABOUT BY GENETICALLY CRISS-CROSSING SOME BREEDS AND THEN INBREEDING THOSE DOGS RESULTING IN THE FACIAL AND NASAL DEFORMITY.” De cramer: “Show ofﬁcials ensure that the breeds indeed conform to the standard - however, there’s many indiv who would say that breed standards in some cases oppose health features.” LINK: THERE IS AN ONGOING BATTLE AGAINST SOME OF THESE REGISTRY BODIES BECAUSE OF CLAIMS THAT THEIR BREED STANDARDS BLATANTLY OPPOSE HEALTH, RATHER THAN PROMOTE IT – THEIR RELUCTANCE TO CHANGE THESE BREED STANDARDS STEMS FROM THE FACT THAT CHANGING FEATURES IN DOGS MAY THREATEN THE VERY EXISTENCE OF THE BREED IN ITS CURRENT FORM. For example the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, bred for a small flat head, is prone to brain damage where the dog scratches and cries out in pain. Dachshunds are bred for length, which can lead to disc and spinal problems. Meg: “When somebody is making money off of this, it’s a commodity, all it needs to do is breed more animals.” NSPCA Spokesperson Meg Wilson says many pedigree dogs become their problem. Meg: “In an overpopulated society why are we encouraging this?” Devi: “Do you think we are obsessed with pedigree dogs and designer dog?” Meg: “I think some people do it for status and they don’t necessarily realize what’s happened behind the scenes.” Vicky Finnemore of the Benoni SPCA responded to a tip off about animal health concerns at a breeder in Johannesburg. VF: “We removed 45 animals with cancerous tumours that had burst open, dental diseases, emaciated dogs that could barely walk, 13 of the dogs had to be put down straight away. The owners of these dogs are international show breed judges, they also breed KUSA registered dogs and sell them to the public.” Francesca and Jackie Browning co-own Braganza and breed poodles, cocker spaniels - and the designer combo - “cocker-poodles” that sell for six to ten thousand rands. Devi: “Did that surprise you?” VF: “No, we have been on plenty cruelty complaints of kusa registered dogs involved.” The Brownings were charged with animal cruelty and neglect, and have been suspended by KUSA. LINK: UNFORTUNATELY, THESE DOGS CAN’T BE ADOPTED UNTIL THE CASE IS FINALIZED AND THAT COULD TAKE YEARS, AND IF THE BROWNINGS ARE FOUND NOT GUILTY, THEN THESE ANIMALS WILL BE RETURNED TO THEM. As the matter is on-going the Brownings declined an interview. UPSOUND: Jacky: “Our statement at this moment in time, is no comment.” Viewers submitted complaints about purebred puppies which have cost them thousands in vet bills, so we investigated some breeders. The first was Sezer Kennels in Randburg, which breeds and shows English bulldogs. It was owned by Arthur Seeff. Photos from 2015 showed injured and dead dogs, leading to animal welfare stepping in and arthur complying with their concerns. Now we received viewers complaints with photos of dogs with serious health issues, spanning the last 20 years: ● Napoleon, and Wellington had spinal issues that led to both being put down, ● Clementine died when her trachea collapsed, ● Patches had severe hip dysplasia and was put down, ● And Jessebel's spinal issues have paralysed her. We paid them a visit undercover. Journalist: “So your dogs are very healthy?” Arthur: ‘We have not got a sick dog on the property and we’ve got 80 dogs here.” Sezer Kennels registers puppies like Arabella with KUSA. A: “This is the girl, but I need her for breeding.” Once Arabella’s show days are over, she’s destined to be bred regularly, just like her mother. Journalist: “How often do they mate?” Arthur: “6 months.” KUSA and several experts say continual breeding is unethical because it doesn’t allow the mother to recover from repeated caesareans. We asked Arthur for an interview: UPSOUND: Arthur Seeff: “I’m in and out of hospital, I’m not in the best frame of mind.” We halted the story to give Arthur time to get well, but he subsequently passed away and there’s been no further comment from his family. Beverlander is another breeding facility selling KUSA registered French and English bulldogs. Our viewers complained that their Randfontein operation owned by Alta Wilters produces puppies with serious genetic issues - like Winston whose long list of health problems resulted in his death before his first birthday. A caring dog lover took in these 5 dogs because they all suffered from a number of different genetic defects - including swimmer syndrome. Wilters declined an on-camera interview, but said that Beverlander isn’t a puppy mill and that the SPCA has found nothing wrong with her dogs’ living conditions. The SPCA says it can do little about the continuous breeding of dogs with genetic disorders. Wilters says she’s one of many breeders dealing with inherent genetic defects of specific breeds. AW: “Am I the only person that that happens to? That dog, it can be in the surroundings where she picked up that sickness.” KUSA’s general manager Pascale Midgley says they’re regulated by the department of agriculture. Pascale Midgley: “There is no such thing as a kusa breeder, we do not license someone to say that you are a breeder.” Devi: “Can anyone breed?” Pascale: “No one can stop anybody from having a litter. The Kennel Union has registered 178,000 dogs over the last 10 years. If we impose very very strict requirements all that happens is that ppl stop registering.” Devi: “As a registry, it’s not your responsibility to go out check facilities? PM: “Under animal improvement act we don’t have that jurisdiction. Devi: “But dogs are your currency you’re not looking necessarily after the welfare of the dogs?” PM: “We not an animal welfare organization, we support them when necessary.” Devi: “Should we not look at changing those breed standards PM: “So the breed standards are evolving, and we automatically adopt those changes.” LINK: ONE STUDY BY THE IMPERIAL COLLEGE OF LONDON SHOWED THAT THE 10,000 PUGS IN THE UK, THEY’RE SO INBRED, THAT THEIR GENE POOL IS THE EQUIVALENT OF ONLY 50 INDIVIDUALS. Canine Geneticist Mischa Fraser of Inqaba laboratory specializes in testing for genetic conditions. MF: “Something that is inherited, is inherited from mother or father to child. So a genetic disease might be inherited.” The lab has developed 700 possible genetic tests that a breeder can use. MF: “We're very involved with many breeders and a breeder will often come and tell me this is the test I'm interested in.” There are ethical breeders like June and Cheryl who are KUSA members and do test their breeding stock to ensure the healthiest dogs possible are bred- but there are no guarantees. To curb bad breeding practices KUSA’s is designing an enhanced registration certificate that shows a puppy has been genetically tested. De Cramer would like to take it a step further: Having an online health registration database with genetic testing results. Dr. DC: “The breeding authorities should still take courageous steps to try and make a lot of things mandatory so that the public out there you know have some sort of a minimum guarantee.” LINK: IN 2017, THE UK’S ANIMAL WELFARE LEGISLATION CHANGED TO INCLUDE A NEW LAW WHICH WILL ALLOW FOR THE PROSECUTION OF BREEDERS WHO KNOWINGLY PRODUCE UNHEALTHY PUPPIES AND KITTENS WITH GENETIC DEFECTS. THIS EFFECTIVELY CREATES THE CRIME OF “QUALZUCHT” OR TORTURE BREEDING . But since South Africa has no laws against unethical breeding practices, Dale Neves set up a bulldog breeding council to help breeders test their breeding stock. Dale: “We are not expecting the breeders to have dogs that are completely healthy, but don't then onsell a dog knowing full well that you’ve bred a dog with hereditary diseases.” Fabio will undergo a lifetime of acupuncture and water therapy sessions to rebuild muscle so he can walk properly. Devi: “Getting a puppy is too much of an impulse purchase?” DR QS: “Yes, it’s an emotional decision, what they don’t realize is that they're supporting that business, and they just made it possible for that breeder to make money. So why will they stop breeding?” THE END

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): When you buy a pedigree and purebred pup you believe you are buying the best and healthiest dogs - but our investigation shows that is not the case.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We are going to be looking the entire industry - from breeding and how it began in Victorian England times, to the dog shows which award breeders with best in show awards for certain bred attributes - which are unhealthy for the dog, to the breeders - both unethical and ethical, and then to the regulator of the industry KUSA. We will interview numerous case studies and go undercover to show the real way this industry works. Based on the UK documentary's which exposed this industry on the UK kennel club, who established these breeds. This is going to rock our audience's socks off - because what you thought was healthy and wonderful - will turn your perception of this world on its head.
metadata.Summary: Riddled with genetic disease Dog breeds aren’t even a real thing – like nature created them that way, and that every mutt is a mix of pure breeds. Like: 1,5 retriever, sheepdog, 1/6 poodle, chow? German shepherd, 1/12 border collie So they are selectively bred for their traits – 90% of all dog breeds were created the past 100 years. In 19th century Victorian era, competitive dog breeding became all the rage…then they declared it a pure breed. Inbred – never allowed to mate outside of species. One study found that 10,000 pugs have the same genetic diversity as 50 individuals – making them highly inbred. This leads to them being often sick. 60% of golden retrievers die of cancer, 1/3 of spaniel’s have skulls too small for their brains. Great Danes are so huge now that their hearts can’t support their bodies. Bulldog – so cute – total genetic failure. A century of inbreeding has ruined them, noses are so squashed they can barely breathe, their heads are so big they can only give birth by caesarean section, their tails have become ingrown, they basically all have hip dysplasia and their average life expectancy is 6 years – these dogs shouldn’t be alive. But they win things like “best in show.” Kennel clubs could fix their problems if they cross breed, but they won’t because then they won’t be as cute. It’s our existence that is letting them live up to our arbitrary existence. Easy solution – go to shelter.

Floris costs R3,600 (special rate for me – and tax is reported to SARS, and comes back to CAP during tax season.) X3 days = R10,800 for Floris. If it’s Jan, I think it’s R4000. So that’s R12,000 Graphic day = R4,500 for graphics to be created by Ethniks. I will need some complicated graphics potentially, so I’m flagging it now. It would be to show the breeding standards, an explanation of how breeders breed, and how a dog is bred for certain traits. I’ve used Owen, he’s also usually happy to drop his rate for me… Audio Mix: Usually take a full day because it’s double the amount of time. R1,026 per hour. Rob usually takes 4 hours for 10 minutes. So R8,208 for the day. I can also chat to rob and make sure he doesn’t go over. I will keep you informed if there any audio issues, but I haven’t had any in the past (touch wood) So roughly: R50, 908 at the maximums of all those figures above. + car hire + Sasha Fuel (which has not been included). For the higher costs Wynand intimated it would be a longer story. I asked for 20 minutes, but obviously it depends on the stuff we have. So far it’s very strong.
